summary: Full-size 1993 copy of the 1922 Hornet Peak cabin at the Missoula Smokejumper Visitor Center; the visitor center page says it is closed for renovations.

facts.design: Full-size copy of the D-1 log cupola cabin at Hornet Peak
facts.status_note: A copy, not the original. The original Hornet Peak lookout is in the Flathead National Forest and is available for rental.

access.note: The Forest Service page, as read, says the visitor center is closed for renovations. Tours are pre-scheduled by email or phone.

events.note: Original Hornet Peak lookout established with a 15-foot pole platform and a log shed.
D-1 log cupola cabin built at Hornet Peak; the original lookout was later abandoned and then restored.
Full-size replica of the Hornet Peak cabin built at the Missoula Smokejumper Visitor Center.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The lookout history page says the copy reproduces the Hornet Peak cabin; a travel listing describes a replica of a 1930s lookout tower. The story gives the specific account and notes the other.
The travel listing describes free tours at set times daily; the Forest Service page says the visitor center is closed for renovations. The story follows the Forest Service page.

sources.title: Smokejumper Visitor Center in Missoula Montana

notes_for_editor: The 1993 build date comes from one source (firelookout.com). The visitor center closure is from the cached Forest Service page, whose date is unknown. A search snippet for a Spanish-language version of the same Forest Service page listed hours by appointment through May 22, 2026, and summer hours from May 26, 2026; I did not confirm that and the cached copy says closed for renovations. Recheck before publishing. On the register list, the line 'National Museum of FS History' sits under the replica row, but it is unclear whether it names the replica's location, so the story does not use it. Original elevation: 6744 ft (firelookout.com) vs 6,737 ft (NHLR). The brief's 'replica at the Missoula Aerial Fire Depot' fits the Travelmt and Forest Service pages.
